summary: Frontend-only retest to verify fix of React 'destroy is not a function' runtime error in UserAccess component. Verified full navigation, auto-refresh cleanup, user creation, and logout. NO React pageerrors and NO console errors detected across entire flow.
critical_code_review_comments: App.js is a single-line dense file (~38 lines but each line 400+ chars). Consider splitting into components/files for maintainability, though not a bug.
useEffect(load, []) anti-pattern was correctly fixed to useEffect(() => { load(); }, []) at line 37.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Bug 'destroy is not a function' is fully resolved. Full E2E frontend flow verified: login -> overview/devices/network/reports/users tabs -> add user -> refresh -> logout. No React runtime errors, no console errors, no webpack overlay. Backend already 100% verified in iteration 3.
rca of the issue: Root cause: React useEffect expects the effect callback to return either undefined or a cleanup function. Original code `useEffect(load, [])` passed an async function directly, which returns a Promise. When React tried to invoke that Promise as a cleanup on unmount, it threw 'destroy is not a function'. Fix: wrap with `useEffect(() => { load(); }, [])` so the effect returns undefined. Verified by navigating away from User access tab (unmount) with no runtime error.
